application_review: Finite powers of convex combinations have an exact independent-index expansion preserving every coefficient. Uniform product correlation bounds transfer with the same error, independently of the number of mixture components.

Finite-support power correlations are continuous in the ambient product topology. Uniform product estimates pass to the closed convex test hull and to every fixed polynomial, including its constant term.

The original signed clipped single-template test class has uniform all-fixed-order product correlations derived from the actual mixed-dual theorem with one unchanged original master family. Signs are factored exactly with absolute product one.

Weierstrass approximation of max(t,0) on the bounded interval and the actual weighted-mass budget derive uniform positive-part correlations on the closed convex hull. Each approximating polynomial is fixed before the stage limit.

Sion minimax is instantiated with compact coordinate cubes, the compact bounded closed convex test hull and actual finite pairings. Continuity and affine-section convexity/concavity are proved, and a positive-part indicator model proves the upper bound from 0<=rho<=nu.

For any fixed original local template, fixed clipping cut above A_d and requested positive error, sufficiently large stages admit a [0,1]-valued model simultaneously approximating all admissible signed clipped inputs, uniformly in 0<=rho<=nu.

Uniform weighted single-dual clipping error is derived from the proved actual clipping limit for arbitrary admissible input sequences. The same selected model then approximates all original untruncated inputs of the fixed template. Heterogeneous-template unions and the single asymptotic model-sequence diagonal remain unproved.

The generic hull and positive-part helpers are concretely instantiated with the original harmonic root law, actual nu block mask, original separately conditioned local prime law and the same quotient shifts and designated denominator.

The all-replica-count signed product application changes only the disjoint global replica-slot arity; original master arity, polynomial list and family are fixed. Local inclusion, denominator membership, positive dimension, admissible tails and gap<=root remain explicit inputs.

The weighted root-mass cap three comes from the previously derived mean-two limit. The centered mask domination is derived from actual mask nonnegativity; neither a positive-part limit nor a dense-model limit is assumed in the actual application.

The closed convex hull is compact in the coordinate product topology as a closed subset of the coordinate interval cube. Sion is applied directly; a minimax identity or saddle point is not an application hypothesis.
The positive-part indicator model is [0,1]-valued and its weighted pairing is at most the centered positive-part pairing, using nonnegative original coefficients and 0<=rho<=nu.

The same model works for all admissible epsilon and vertex tests of one fixed original local template and its prescribed gap/J-choice sequence, after selecting one requested error. Separate fixed-template model existence does not prove a common model for a union of heterogeneous original templates or all J0 choices.
The final uniform original approximation retains the actual untruncated dual in the pairing. The bound |rho-model|<=1+nu and the derived uniform weighted clipping error perform the transfer.

No single model sequence satisfying all errors or slowly growing J0 has been chosen. The full preprint dense-model proposition, concrete correlation templates, Prediction/Alignment and StrongConjecture remain unfinished.
